model_run: SFINCS v4_refreeze naccs-premier (preliminary, Hurricane Sandy 28-31 Oct 2012)

high_water_marks.estimator: model peak water level = median over the model within 50 m of each mark
high_water_marks.scored_rule: USGS quality 2 or better (q<=2); a mark the model leaves dry is scored against ground
high_water_marks.bias_meaning: median(model - observed); negative = model a little low

flood_extent.what: agreement with FEMA MOTF observed Sandy surge extent (Critical Success Index, 1 = perfect)
flood_extent.excluded_note: areas where the FEMA layer is not valid (outside New Jersey) are excluded

gauge_sign_conventions: peak_error_m = model peak - observed peak (m); peak_timing_error_min = model peak time - observed peak time (positive = model late)

gauges.name: Sandy Hook, NJ
gauges.note: Gauge was destroyed on the rising tide before Sandy's peak (last reading 10-29 23:00 UTC); errors compare the model with the gauge up to that moment only.

gauges.name: Newark Bay at PVSC, NJ
gauges.note: Gauge record has a gap after the peak (10-30 04:00 to 10-31 17:12 UTC).

gauges.name: Atlantic City (Steel Pier), NJ
gauges.note: Model peak is about half a metre too high here, the largest gauge miss; the pre-storm tide lines up, so this is not a datum problem.

gauges.name: Lewes, DE
gauges.note: Close to where the model is forced with ocean water levels, so a check on the input more than on the model.

gauges.name: Burlington, NJ
gauges.note: NOAA publishes no NAVD88 datum for this gauge; its NAVD88 level is derived from MLLW plus neighbouring gauges (approximate).
